original_question: For probability tensors, determine which counts of real critical points can occur among the aEDdeg(S_{n1,...,nd}) critical points.
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Problem 13 (“Best low rank approximations”), motivated immediately by the quoted statement from [BPS22, Conj. 20].
correct_elements: Your draft already pinpoints the right local target: Section 2.4’s Problem 13. It correctly focuses on probability tensors, on counting real critical points, and on the affine Euclidean distance degree notation aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}). It is also close to the paper’s own wording: the paper asks to “determine the possible numbers of real elements among the aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}) critical points of a probability tensor.”
missing_details: The notation S_{n_1,...,n_d} should be defined: it is the affine cone over the Segre variety of rank-one tensors in P(V_1 \otimes ... \otimes V_d), with dim V_i = n_i + 1.
The critical points are not arbitrary critical points of the tensor; they are critical points of the Euclidean distance optimization problem to the affine variety of rank-one probability tensors.
The paper’s local definition of a probability tensor should be made explicit: it is a tensor whose entries lie in the affine hyperplane given by the condition that the sum of all entries is 1.

The count aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}) is the generic complex count of critical points for the affine Euclidean distance problem; this genericity/finite-distinctness assumption is implicit in your draft and should be stated.
“Real critical points” should be clarified to mean those critical points among the complex critical set whose coordinates are real.
The quantifier should be explicit: the problem asks which integers occur as the number of real critical points as the probability tensor varies.

The nearby motivation from [BPS22, Conj. 20] is narrower than your draft: for probability tensors with nonnegative coordinates, the conjecture is that exactly one of those critical points is real. Problem 13 then asks for the full range of possible counts more generally.

Ambient-field context is implicit in your draft: the notes work mainly over the complex numbers, while the question singles out the real locus. No homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is part of this target problem.
refined_question: Fix real inner-product spaces V_1,...,V_d with dim V_i = n_i + 1, and let S_{n_1,...,n_d} be the affine cone over the Segre variety of rank-one tensors in P(V_1 \otimes ... \otimes V_d). Call T in V_1 \otimes ... \otimes V_d a probability tensor if the sum of its entries is 1. For such a tensor T, consider the affine Euclidean distance problem from T to the variety of rank-one probability tensors S_{n_1,...,n_d} \cap {sum of entries = 1}; for generic T this problem has aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}) complex critical points. As T varies over probability tensors, which integers can occur as the number of these critical points whose entries are real?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 13, not the neighboring Problem 12: Problem 12 asks for existence of tensors whose entire singular-tuple critical set is real, whereas your draft asks for the possible counts of real critical points among the affine Euclidean-distance critical points. The paper itself introduces EDdeg and aEDdeg in Section 2.4, defines S_{n_1,...,n_d} there, explains that probability tensors lie in the affine hyperplane where the sum of entries is 1, quotes [BPS22, Conj. 20] in the nonnegative-coordinate case, and then immediately states Problem 13 in essentially the same terms as your draft. The main omissions in the draft are definitional and quantificational: what S_{n_1,...,n_d} is, what optimization problem the critical points come from, what “probability tensor” means in this paper, and that aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}) is the generic complex count. No broader reformulation is needed.
